# Second Critique — Real Door, Not Decorative XML

The Awtsmoos opens a door only when a crawler can walk through what it names; Awtsmoos.com therefore needs discovery links, canonical documents, and production truth in the same frame.

## Improvement over the earlier sitemap idea

The sitemap is not the entire crawl graph. It is the seed.

The real crawl architecture is:

`robots.txt`
→ root sitemap + Heichel seed sitemap
→ public Heichel roots
→ server-rendered child-series links
→ server-rendered child-series / stable named-post links
→ server-rendered Torah article with canonical metadata

This avoids giant recursive sitemap latency while still making the Torah graph discoverable through standard `<a href>` links.

## Release architecture

Because the shared main worktree is dirty, create an isolated worktree from the current local `main` commit—not from stale `origin/main`. Copy only the reviewed SEO files into that release worktree. Test there. Commit there on a temporary release branch. Then fast-forward local `main` to that exact commit only if its original HEAD has not diverged unexpectedly. Push `main` after a fresh fetch/fast-forward ancestry check.

This preserves every existing committed local-main change while excluding unrelated uncommitted work.
